authority_binding.current_semantics: verifies bound main path and st_dev/st_ino, then hashes only canonical_db_path+db_device+db_inode into authority_receipt_sha256

recovery_guard.current_semantics: st_dev/st_ino check before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then typed checkpoint/digest/provenance/CAS checks

static_identity_probe.current_semantics: main-file SHA-256 and schema metadata under mode=ro&immutable=1; explicitly excludes uncheckpointed WAL state and is explicitly not a full state snapshot

architecture_decision.reason: File identity answers which durable file is authoritative; SQLite revision witnessing answers whether that same file/database has advanced since this connection established its trusted epoch. They are different predicates and should stay separate.

minimal_python_native_candidate.name: EXTERNAL_SQLITE_REVISION_FENCE/v1
minimal_python_native_candidate.baseline: PRAGMA main.data_version captured on the long-lived CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore connection after path/device/inode binding
minimal_python_native_candidate.guard: Before a recovery or other authority-sensitive mutation, compare PRAGMA main.data_version on the same connection to the baseline and fail closed on change.
minimal_python_native_candidate.why_own_store_writes_do_not_false_positi: SQLite specifies PRAGMA data_version as unchanged for commits made on that same connection.
minimal_python_native_candidate.wal_relevance: External WAL commits are database changes even while the main-file inode remains unchanged; E3 must prove the exact Python/runtime behavior before build adoption.
minimal_python_native_candidate.schema_classification: PRAGMA main.schema_version may be sampled as a diagnostic classifier when drift is detected, but it must not become a second authority or be application-written.

threat_scope_split.candidate: PRAGMA data_version on the persistent store connection
threat_scope_split.covers: committed changes by other SQLite connections/processes, including expected WAL cases subject to reproduction
threat_scope_split.does_not_claim: arbitrary mutation through the exact same sqlite3.Connection object

threat_scope_split.candidate: either explicit connection encapsulation plus brokered mutation accounting, or a later native SQLITE_FCNTL_DATA_VERSION bridge
threat_scope_split.reason: PRAGMA data_version deliberately omits same-connection writes; Python stdlib sqlite3 exposes total_changes but no documented sqlite3_file_control wrapper was found in the current 3.14 API surface. total_changes also has row-count/rollback/DDL semantics that make it unsuitable for silent promotion into canonical revision identity.

threat_scope_split.candidate: not solved by a connection-local counter alone
threat_scope_split.reason: pager counters are drift witnesses, not cryptographic state attestations

rejected_shortcuts: Do not rerun fingerprint_unifieddb as a live guard: its immutable=1 probe explicitly disables change detection and excludes uncheckpointed WAL state.
Do not make the full mutable UnifiedDBFingerprint receipt canonical again; G3/G4 intentionally migrated away from that unstable representation.
Do not use mtime/size as a substitute for SQLite logical revision.
Do not make schema_version the general drift counter.
Do not add APSW/ctypes/native-pointer extraction merely to reach SQLITE_FCNTL_DATA_VERSION before the pure-Python discriminator is tested.
Do not reopen or modify accepted G4 repeat-provenance semantics unless a new executable post-G4 counterexample hits the separate same-inode lane.

next_experiment_design.surface: isolated temporary SQLite fixture, not target VPS and not Frankenstein runtime credit
cases: no-change control: same store connection, data_version stable
second-connection committed DML in DELETE/rollback journal mode: data_version expected change
second-connection committed DML in WAL mode with same main-file inode: data_version expected change
second-connection committed DDL: data_version expected change and schema_version expected change
verify main-file st_dev/st_ino remains equal across all cases
keep any connection-close/reopen result separately scoped because data_version values are only comparable on the same connection
next_experiment_design.falsifier: If an external committed WAL DML can leave PRAGMA data_version unchanged on the same long-lived observer connection, reject G5A and escalate to a stronger native/snapshot mechanism.
